description: Declares per-group creative requirements that each offering must satisfy. Allows formats to specify what asset groups (headlines, images, videos) offerings must provide, along with count and per-asset technical constraints.

examples.description: Landscape image constraint with count bounds

asset_group_id.description: The asset group this constraint applies to. Values are canonical-format vocabulary — each declaration chooses its own group IDs (e.g., 'headlines', 'images', 'videos'). Buyers discover them through Product.format_options[], publisher adagents.json formats[], or creative.supported_formats[] according to context.

anyOf.description: Requirements for image creative assets. These define the technical constraints for image files.

animation_allowed.description: Whether animated images (GIF, animated WebP) are accepted

bleed.description: Required bleed area beyond the trim size. The submitted image must be larger than the declared dimensions: total width = trim width + left bleed + right bleed, total height = trim height + top bleed + bottom bleed. For uniform bleed: total = trim + (2 * uniform). Uses the same unit as the parent dimensions.

uniform.description: Same bleed on all four sides

color_space.description: Required color space. Print typically requires CMYK.

max_animation_duration_ms.description: Maximum animation duration in milliseconds (if animation_allowed is true)

max_height.description: Maximum height. Interpretation depends on unit (default: pixels). For exact dimensions, set min_height = max_height.

max_weight_grams.description: Maximum weight in grams for the finished physical piece (print inserts, flyers). Affects postage calculations and production constraints. Only applicable to print channels.

max_width.description: Maximum width. Interpretation depends on unit (default: pixels). For exact dimensions, set min_width = max_width.

min_dpi.description: Minimum resolution in dots per inch. Always in DPI regardless of the dimension unit. Standard print requires 300 DPI, newspaper 150 DPI.

min_height.description: Minimum height. Interpretation depends on unit (default: pixels). For exact dimensions, set min_height = max_height.

min_width.description: Minimum width. Interpretation depends on unit (default: pixels). For exact dimensions, set min_width = max_width.

parameters_from_format_id.description: When true on a legacy template format, logical width, logical height, and pixel ratio are supplied by the parameterized format_id. The image asset's intrinsic dimensions MUST equal logical dimensions multiplied by pixel_ratio (which defaults to 1 when omitted).

pixel_ratios.description: Accepted intrinsic-pixel densities for this image slot. One submitted image matching any listed ratio satisfies the slot; the array does not require one asset per ratio. Absence imposes no density constraint beyond the existing dimension requirements.

transparency_required.description: Whether the image must support transparency (requires PNG, WebP, or GIF)

unit.description: Unit of measurement for width/height values. Defaults to 'px' when absent. Print formats use 'inches' or 'cm'.
unit.title: Dimension Unit

anyOf.title: Image Asset Requirements

anyOf.description: Requirements for video creative assets. These define the technical constraints for video files.

items.description: Audio channel configuration for audio and video assets
items.title: Audio Channel Layout

audio_required.description: Whether the video must include an audio track

audio_sample_rates.description: Accepted audio sample rates in Hz (e.g., [44100, 48000])

frame_rate_type.description: Required frame rate type. Broadcast and SSAI require constant frame rate for seamless splicing.

enumDescriptions.constant: Constant frame rate (CFR) — each frame occupies an identical time interval
enumDescriptions.variable: Variable frame rate (VFR) — frame intervals may differ

frame_rate_type.title: Frame Rate Type

frame_rates.description: Accepted frame rates in frames per second (e.g., [24, 30, 60])

gop_type.description: Required GOP structure. SSAI and broadcast require closed GOPs for clean splice points.

enumDescriptions.closed: Each GOP is independently decodable — required for SSAI and broadcast splicing
enumDescriptions.open: GOPs may reference frames from adjacent GOPs — not suitable for splicing

gop_type.title: GOP Type

loudness_lufs.description: Target integrated loudness in LUFS (e.g., -24 for broadcast, -16 for streaming)

loudness_tolerance_db.description: Acceptable deviation from loudness_lufs target in dB (e.g., 2 means -22 to -26 LUFS for a -24 target)

max_bitrate_kbps.description: Maximum video bitrate in kilobits per second

max_file_size_kb.description: Maximum file size, where 1 KB is exactly 1,000 bytes

max_gop_interval_seconds.description: Maximum keyframe interval in seconds. SSAI typically requires 1-2 second intervals.

min_bitrate_kbps.description: Minimum video bitrate in kilobits per second

moov_atom_position.description: Required moov atom position in MP4 container. 'start' enables progressive download without buffering the entire file.

enumDescriptions.end: moov atom at end of file — requires full download before playback can begin
enumDescriptions.start: moov atom at beginning of file — enables progressive download and streaming delivery

moov_atom_position.title: Moov Atom Position

scan_type.description: Required scan type. Modern delivery requires progressive scan.

enumDescriptions.interlaced: Alternating lines drawn in two passes per frame (legacy broadcast)
enumDescriptions.progressive: All lines of each frame are drawn in sequence

scan_type.title: Scan Type

true_peak_dbfs.description: Maximum true peak level in dBFS (e.g., -2 for broadcast)

anyOf.title: Video Asset Requirements

loudness_lufs.description: Target integrated loudness in LUFS. LKFS is the equivalent unit name under ITU-R BS.1770; values expressed in LUFS and LKFS are directly comparable without conversion.

loudness_tolerance_db.description: Acceptable deviation from the loudness_lufs target in dB.

max_bitrate_kbps.description: Maximum audio bitrate in kilobits per second

min_bitrate_kbps.description: Minimum audio bitrate in kilobits per second

anyOf.description: Requirements for text creative assets such as headlines, body copy, and CTAs.

allowed_values.description: Closed set of permitted string values for this text slot. When present, a conformant implementation MUST reject any submitted content not in this list with `CREATIVE_VALUE_NOT_ALLOWED` (echoing the offending field path in `error.field` and the allowed list in `error.details.allowed_values`). Matching is case-sensitive; producers MUST supply exact casing. If the submitted value contains unresolved template tokens (e.g., {{product_name}}), validation against allowed_values MUST be deferred until interpolation is complete. All declared constraints (allowed_values, character_pattern, max_length, etc.) are conjunctive — submitted content must satisfy every applicable constraint simultaneously.

prohibited_terms.description: List of prohibited words or phrases

anyOf.title: Text Asset Requirements

anyOf.description: Requirements for HTML creative assets. These define the execution environment constraints that the HTML must be compatible with.

allowed_external_domains.description: List of domains the HTML creative may reference for external resources. Only applicable when external_resources_allowed is true.

external_resources_allowed.description: Whether the HTML creative can load external resources (scripts, images, fonts, etc.). When false, all resources must be inlined or bundled.

max_file_size_kb.description: Maximum file size in kilobytes for the HTML asset

sandbox.description: Sandbox environment the HTML must be compatible with. 'none' = direct DOM access, 'iframe' = standard iframe isolation, 'safeframe' = IAB SafeFrame container, 'fencedframe' = Privacy Sandbox fenced frame

anyOf.title: HTML Asset Requirements

anyOf.description: Requirements for JavaScript creative assets. These define the execution environment constraints that the JavaScript must be compatible with.

allowed_external_domains.description: List of domains the JavaScript may reference for external resources. Only applicable when external_resources_allowed is true.

external_resources_allowed.description: Whether the JavaScript can load external resources dynamically

max_file_size_kb.description: Maximum file size in kilobytes for the JavaScript asset

module_type.description: Required JavaScript module format. 'script' = classic script, 'module' = ES modules, 'iife' = immediately invoked function expression

strict_mode_required.description: Whether the JavaScript must use strict mode

anyOf.title: JavaScript Asset Requirements

anyOf.description: Requirements for VAST (Video Ad Serving Template) creative assets.

media_file_requirements.description: Technical acceptance constraints for the alternative MediaFile renditions in each applicable resolved InLine linear creative.

codecs.description: Accepted codec identifiers for `MediaFile@codec`, using the codec syntax referenced by the applicable VAST version. A missing codec attribute does not satisfy a declared codec constraint unless safe inspection establishes the codec.

containers.description: Accepted normalized container identifiers, such as `mp4`, `webm`, or `mpeg_ts`. A receiver MUST determine the container from authoritative metadata or safe byte inspection and MUST NOT guess it only from the media URI suffix.

delivery_methods.description: Accepted values of the required `MediaFile@delivery` attribute. `progressive` identifies a directly downloadable media file; `streaming` identifies a streaming media resource.

items.description: Delivery method declared by the required VAST MediaFile `delivery` attribute.
items.title: VAST Media Delivery Method

max_bitrate_kbps.description: Maximum accepted MediaFile bitrate in kilobits per second. A fixed `MediaFile@bitrate` must not exceed this value. For adaptive/streaming media, the declared `MediaFile@maxBitrate` must not exceed this value. Safe byte inspection may establish the value when metadata is absent.

max_file_size_bytes.description: Maximum accepted MediaFile size in exact bytes. `MediaFile@fileSize`, when present, is expressed in bytes; a receiver MAY verify it against safely fetched media bytes and MUST use the verified byte count if the values disagree.

mime_types.description: Accepted MIME types from `MediaFile@type`, compared case-insensitively after trimming optional whitespace. Parameters are not accepted in this field. Examples: `video/mp4`, `video/webm`, `audio/mpeg`, `audio/aac`.

min_bitrate_kbps.description: Minimum accepted MediaFile bitrate in kilobits per second. A fixed `MediaFile@bitrate` must be at least this value. For adaptive/streaming media, the declared `MediaFile@minBitrate` must be at least this value. Safe byte inspection may establish the value when metadata is absent.

media_file_requirements.title: VAST MediaFile Requirements

verifier_constraints.adaptive_bitrate_containment: A MediaFile advertising a minBitrate/maxBitrate interval satisfies declared bitrate bounds only when its entire interval is contained within those bounds; overlap alone is insufficient.
verifier_constraints.alternative_renditions: For each applicable resolved InLine linear creative, at least one MediaFile MUST satisfy every declared property in this object; requirements MUST NOT be satisfied by combining properties from different MediaFile elements.
verifier_constraints.missing_metadata: If a declared property cannot be established from VAST metadata or safe inspection, compatibility is unproven and the MediaFile does not satisfy that property.
verifier_constraints.range_order: When both bounds are declared, min_width MUST be <= max_width, min_height MUST be <= max_height, and min_bitrate_kbps MUST be <= max_bitrate_kbps.

vast_version.$comment: VAST 4.3 ships no XSD of its own: IAB's `vast_4.2.xsd` remains the authoritative schema for 4.3 documents, so a validator MUST NOT reject a tag declaring `version="4.3"` for want of a 4.3 schema. VAST 4.4 is deliberately absent because `vast_4.4.xsd` is annotated 'DRAFT for working group discussion' and is not a published specification; add it once IAB publishes it, not before. This file is the single source of truth for the roster, per the Enum Consolidation rule in docs/spec-guidelines.md, and other schemas `$ref` it rather than restating the list.
vast_version.description: Deprecated one-element alias for `vast_versions`. Producers use either the singular legacy alias or the plural 3.2 field, never both.
vast_version.title: VAST Version

vast_versions.description: Accepted VAST version set for this asset requirement.

anyOf.description: Requirements for URL assets such as click-through URLs, tracking pixels, and landing pages.

allowed_domains.description: List of allowed domains for the URL

macro_support.description: Coarse slot gate for macro-bearing URLs. `false` is a hard prohibition on macro tokens. `true` permits tokens but does not prove any dialect semantic, resolver, context, or encoding capability; exact support comes from the selected format option's macro_resolution_capabilities.

protocols.description: Allowed URL protocols. HTTPS is recommended for all ad URLs.

role.description: Purpose this URL slot serves in the format — distinct from `url_type` on the manifest-side asset (which declares the receiver's invocation mechanism). A slot can be `click_tracker` (purpose) and accept a `tracker_pixel` (mechanism) URL, or `clickthrough` (purpose) and accept a `clickthrough` (mechanism) URL. Complements `asset_role` (human-readable label) by providing a machine-readable enum and serves as the receiver's fallback signal when a manifest URL asset omits `url_type`.

anyOf.title: URL Asset Requirements

asset_requirements.description: Technical requirements for each item in this group (e.g., max_length for text, min_width/aspect_ratio for images). Applies uniformly to all items in the group.
asset_requirements.title: Asset Requirements

asset_type.description: The expected content type for this group.
asset_type.title: Asset Content Type

ext.description: Extension object for platform-specific, vendor-namespaced parameters. Extensions are always optional and must be namespaced under a vendor/platform key (e.g., ext.gam, ext.roku). Used for custom capabilities, partner-specific configuration, and features being proposed for standardization.
ext.title: Extension Object

max_count.description: Maximum number of items allowed in this group.

min_count.description: Minimum number of items required in this group.

required.description: Whether this asset group must be present in each offering. Defaults to true.
